text:
---
name: rfe.submit
description: Submit or update RFEs in Jira. Creates new RHAIRFE tickets for new RFEs, or updates existing tickets for RFEs fetched from Jira. Use when reviewed RFE artifacts are ready to be created or updated in Jira, after /rfe.review.
user-invocable: true
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash
---

You are an RFE submission assistant. Your job is to create or update RHAIRFE Jira tickets from reviewed RFE artifacts.

All submission goes through Python scripts that use the Jira REST API directly with Basic Auth (`JIRA_SERVER`, `JIRA_USER`, `JIRA_TOKEN` env vars), not the Atlassian MCP server. This ensures the exact sequence of Jira API calls is deterministic and not dependent on LLM tool-calling decisions.

**This skill is non-interactive.** Do not prompt the user for confirmation before submitting. The user invoked `/rfe.submit` — that is the confirmation. Run the script directly without asking "are you sure?" or presenting a dry run for approval.

## Step 0: Check Credentials

Check if `JIRA_SERVER`, `JIRA_USER`, and `JIRA_TOKEN` environment variables are set. If not, tell the user:

> RFE submission requires Jira API credentials. Set these environment variables:
> ```
> export JIRA_SERVER=https://your-site.atlassian.net
> export JIRA_USER=your-email@example.com
> export JIRA_TOKEN=«redacted»
> ```
> To create an API token, go to https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
>
> After environment variables are set, re-run `/rfe.submit`.

## Step 0.5: Repair Review Frontmatter Invariants

Every label below is derived from review frontmatter, and that frontmatter was written
by several agents across several review cycles, so it drifts into self-contradictions:
`pass` disagreeing with the sum of `scores`, `auto_revised: false` on a review whose
`before_score` differs from `score`, `pass: true` beside `recommendation:
autorevise_reject`. Submitting those mislabels the ticket.

Run this command exactly as written, before Step 1, on every invocation — including
`--dry-run`. It reads every review, writes only the files that violate an invariant,
and prints `REPAIRED <file> <fields>` for each. Never inspect or repair these fields by
hand, and never skip it because the reviews look fine — it is a no-op when they are:

```bash
python3 -c "
import glob,subprocess,yaml
C='what why open_to_how not_a_task right_sized'.split()
for f in sorted(glob.glob('artifacts/rfe-reviews/*-review.md')):
    t=open(f).read()
    if not t.startswith('---'): continue
    m=yaml.safe_load(t[3:t.find('\n---',3)]) or {}
    s=m.get('scores') or {}; d={}; p=m.get('pass'); r=m.get('recommendation','')
    if all(s.get(c) is not None for c in C):
        p=sum(s[c] for c in C)>=7 and 0 not in s.values()
        if m.get('pass')!=p: d['pass']=str(p).lower()
    if not m.get('auto_revised') and (m.get('before_score') not in (None,m.get('score')) or m.get('before_scores') not in (None,s)): d['auto_revised']='true'
    if p and r=='revise' and not m.get('needs_attention'): d['needs_attention']='true'
    if p and (r=='autorevise_reject' or (r=='reject' and m.get('feasibility')!='infeasible')): d.update(recommendation='submit',needs_attention='true')
    if not p and r=='submit': d['recommendation']='revise'
    if m.get('feasibility')=='infeasible' and r=='submit': d['recommendation']='reject'
    if d: subprocess.run(['python3','scripts/frontmatter.py','set',f]+['%s=%s'%i for i in d.items()]); print('REPAIRED',f,d)
print('INVARIANTS OK')
"
```

The five invariants it enforces, in the order it applies them:

1. `pass` is `true` only when `sum(scores.*) >= 7` **and** no `scores.*` is `0`.
2. `before_score != score` (or `before_scores != scores`) proves a revision ran, so
   `auto_revised` must be `true`.
3. A passing review may not recommend `autorevise_reject`, or `reject` without
   `feasibility: infeasible` — it becomes `submit` with `needs_attention: true`.
4. A passing review that recommends `revise` keeps that recommendation but must carry
   `needs_attention: true`.
5. A failing review, or an `infeasible` one, may not recommend `submit`.

Worked example — a file reads `score: 9, before_score: 10, pass: false,
recommendation: autorevise_reject, auto_revised: false, scores: {what:2, why:1,
open_to_how:2, not_a_task:2, right_sized:2}`. The command prints
`REPAIRED … {'pass': 'true', 'auto_revised': 'true', 'recommendation': 'submit',
'needs_attention': 'true'}`: the scores sum to 9 with no zero so it passes (1), the
score moved from 10 so a revision ran (2), and a passing review cannot be an
`autorevise_reject` (3). A file already satisfying all five is left untouched.

## Step 1: Run Submission

```bash
python3 scripts/submit.py [--dry-run] [--artifacts-dir artifacts]
```

## Step 2: Report Results

After the script completes, read `artifacts/rfes.md` (rebuilt by the script) and report the results.

If the script fails, report the error and suggest the user check credentials or use `--dry-run` to validate locally.

## Labeling Scheme

The scripts automatically apply labels based on what happened during the pipeline:

| Label | When applied |
|-------|-------------|
| `rfe-creator-auto-created` | Ticket was created by the pipeline (new RFEs, not updates) |
| `rfe-creator-auto-revised` | Ticket content was modified by automation (review frontmatter `auto_revised: true`) |
| `rfe-creator-split-original` | Parent ticket that was decomposed into smaller RFEs |
| `rfe-creator-split-result` | Child ticket produced by splitting another RFE |
| `rfe-creator-needs-attention` | Automation couldn't fully resolve all issues — human review needed (review frontmatter `needs_attention: true`) |
| `rfe-creator-autofix-rubric-pass` | RFE passed review (recommendation = "submit") — excluded from future auto-fix JQL queries |
| `rfe-creator-feasibility-pass` | Technical feasibility check returned `feasible` |
| `rfe-creator-feasibility-fail` | Technical feasibility check returned `infeasible` |
| `rfe-creator-feasibility-unknown` | Technical feasibility check returned `indeterminate` |

The three `rfe-creator-feasibility-*` labels are mutually exclusive: on each submit, the matching label is added and any others present in the ticket's `original_labels` are removed. Rejected RFEs have any feasibility labels stripped (no add).
